must_not_say: Do not assume the reader has suffered an outage, missed-email complaint, or delivery incident.

emails.status_quo: Checks the platform's own Auth logs in the dashboard to verify whether the documented email limit was actually exceeded.

emails.call_to_action: Read the webhook documentation and register a publicly accessible endpoint for `email.delivered`: https://resend.com/features/webhooks
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether capturing a delivery event provides the operational visibility needed for the reader's transactional email workflow.
emails.next_step_value: The documentation shows the first setup action: register a publicly accessible endpoint, select `email.delivered`, and receive the event as a JSON POST request.
emails.next_step_limit: This first step demonstrates how to receive a delivery notification; it does not establish inbox placement, recipient engagement, or production behavior for the reader's specific environment.

events.subject: Inspect delivery after a send
events.preview_text: Capture a separate delivery signal with one webhook event.
events.body:
Resend webhooks let you inspect what happens after a transactional email is sent. A successful send request covers the request itself; delivery is a separate event worth capturing.

Resend sends real-time email events to your registered endpoint as JSON POST requests. This gives you a concrete signal to inspect outside the original send request.

Start with one documented setup step: register a publicly accessible endpoint and select `email.delivered` as the event type. When the event occurs, Resend sends its details to your route.

Use that first event to decide whether delivery notifications provide the operational visibility your transactional email workflow needs. It confirms receipt of a delivery event—not inbox placement or recipient engagement.

events.subject: Inspect delivery after sending
events.preview_text: Capture a separate delivery notification with one webhook event.
events.body:
A successful send request confirms the request succeeded. It does not describe the message’s later delivery state.

Resend webhooks send real-time email events to your server as JSON POST requests. Capturing `email.delivered` gives you a separate delivery notification to inspect after the original request.

Start with one event. In the webhook documentation, register a publicly accessible endpoint and select `email.delivered`. Resend will POST the event details to that route as JSON.

This first step shows how a delivery notification reaches your endpoint. It does not establish inbox placement or recipient engagement, but it lets you evaluate whether delivery events provide useful operational visibility for your transactional email workflow.

events.arc: Move the reader from knowing only that a send was initiated to seeing how an `email.delivered` event can make delivery status inspectable, then let them verify the documented setup prerequisites before proceeding.

emails.job: Get the reader to recognize the practical value of inspecting delivery events and check whether they can satisfy the documented prerequisites for a first Resend evaluation.
emails.single_idea: A successful send request is not the end of the delivery path. Resend can post an `email.delivered` event as JSON to a registered endpoint, giving the engineer a concrete event to inspect; before setting that up, the documented first step is to confirm access to a Resend API key and a verified domain.
must_not_say: Do not assume the reader has experienced an outage, missing email, or delivery incident.
Do not assume a current email provider, authentication platform, framework, language, or integration stack.
Do not claim that an `email.delivered` event proves inbox placement, opens, or recipient engagement.
Do not imply that the CLI quickstart configures webhooks or removes the need for a publicly accessible endpoint.
Do not claim that an API key and verified domain alone validate webhook behavior or production delivery.
Do not promise detection of an upstream platform wiping SMTP configuration or explain another platform's rate-limit accounting.
Do not introduce pricing, plan limits, migration claims, customer proof, marketing email, or unrelated Resend features.
emails.felt_need: Auth email sending (signup confirmation, OTP, magic link, invites) gets blocked with a 429 email rate limit error under normal usage, even when the reporter believes they are under the documented limit.
emails.status_quo: Checks the platform's own Auth logs in the dashboard to verify whether the documented email limit was actually exceeded.
emails.mechanism: Resend sends real-time email events to a registered endpoint as JSON POST requests, including `email.delivered`. The CLI quickstart provides a narrow readiness check by documenting that getting started requires a Resend API key and a verified domain.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether the reader is ready to proceed with a Resend webhook evaluation or first needs to obtain an API key or verify a domain.
emails.next_step_value: The public quickstart states the two requirements for getting started: a Resend API key and a verified domain.
emails.next_step_limit: This page establishes CLI setup prerequisites; it does not configure a webhook endpoint, demonstrate `email.delivered`, or validate behavior in the reader's production environment.

events.subject: Inspect delivery events with Resend
events.preview_text: See the JSON event that follows a transactional send.
events.body:
Resend lets you inspect what happens after a transactional email is sent. A successful send request is not the end of the delivery path.

With webhooks, Resend posts real-time email events as JSON to a registered, publicly accessible endpoint. An `email.delivered` event gives you a concrete delivery signal to inspect without implying inbox placement, an open, or recipient engagement.

Before setting up an endpoint, confirm that you have the two documented prerequisites: a Resend API key and a verified domain.

Check the prerequisites: https://resend.com/docs/cli-quickstart

This readiness check does not configure or test a webhook. It tells you whether you can proceed with an evaluation or need to obtain an API key or verify a domain first.

events.preview_text: See the JSON event available after a transactional email is delivered.
events.body:
Resend can send real-time email events to a registered endpoint as JSON POST requests. That gives you a specific event to inspect after a transactional send instead of treating the send request as the end of the delivery path.

An email.delivered event provides a concrete delivery signal. It does not establish inbox placement, an open, or recipient engagement.

Before configuring a webhook, confirm that you have the two prerequisites listed in the Resend CLI quickstart: access to a Resend API key and a verified domain. The page establishes those setup requirements; it does not configure or validate a webhook endpoint.

If both are available, you can decide whether you are ready to proceed with a webhook evaluation.
